drhp.business: The Company is engaged in only one segment, namely the manufacture and sale of gelatine and related products like ossein and di-calcium phosphate (DCP), and accordingly reports no separate segments under Ind AS-108. Gelatine accounted for 70.77% of turnover and DCP 29.15% during the year under review. Its gelatine goes into applications the Company describes across food and beverage, pharmaceuticals (hard and soft capsules, tablet coating, syrups), cosmetics, photography and nutraceuticals.

risks.note: Management names this as the primary market barrier: 'The rise of plant-based gelatin substitutes, fueled by rising demand for vegetarian and vegan goods, is one of the primary market barriers. Traditional gelatin made from animal sources is affected due to this trend'. It attacks the core product rather than a segment, so it is structural for a single-product gelatine maker.
risks.risk: Substitution by plant-based gelatin alternatives, plus cultural and religious prohibitions on animal-source gelatine

risks.note: The cautionary statement lists 'raw material availability, import and exports of raw material and finished goods' among the factors outside the Company's control. The FY26 benefit came from a global gelatine price fall in the second half that cut raw-material cost and let the Company import at competitive prices, easing 'pressure in domestic raw material supplies' - the same mechanism reverses if global prices rise.
risks.risk: Raw material availability and price, including reliance on imports versus domestic supply

risks.note: 'The Company is engaged in only one segment, namely, manufacture and sale of gelatine and related products like assein and di-calcium phosphate (DCP) and as such there are no reportable segments as per Ind AS-108.' With gelatine 70.77% and DCP 29.15% of turnover, there is no diversification to absorb a shock to gelatine demand or pricing.

During FY2025-26 gelatine sales volume rose 16.17% but the average selling price of gelatine fell 5.20%; DCP volume rose 11.35% with its average selling price up 17.17%. The gelatine price direction is set by the global market, not by the Company, so volume gains can be offset by realisation.
risks.risk: Gelatine realisation deflation - price risk decoupling volume growth from revenue

risks.note: Power and fuel cost fell 4.98% 'due to decrease in the coal prices and consumption', and profit growth was attributed to 'better yield and lower consumption of power and fuel'. A material part of the FY26 margin expansion is therefore a commodity input tailwind that can reverse.
risks.risk: Energy and fuel cost exposure, principally coal

risks.note: 'Prolonged geopolitical instability, including the middle-east conflict, may continue to impact global trade flows and overall market sentiments.' This bears on both imported raw material and exports, which grew sharply in FY26.
risks.risk: Geopolitical instability affecting global trade flows

risks.note: The cautionary statement lists 'government regulations, changes in taxation' among factors that could make a significant difference to operations and over which the Company has no direct control. The business is also subject to food-safety, pollution-control, legal-metrology and factories legislation per the secretarial audit scope.

The forward-looking-statement caveat names 'economic conditions, affecting demand and supply ... natural calamities, on which the Company does not have any direct control' as reasons actual results may differ from stated expectations.
risks.risk: Demand and macro conditions plus natural calamities outside management control
